world.h: UN condemns US embargo of Cuba as support slips
world.b: The General Assembly vote was 130-17 with 25 abstentions, down from more than 160 nations last year, as Germany and Italy were among those that refrained.
world.title: UN condemns U.S. economic embargo of Cuba though more nations sit out amid Trump push

world.h: Trump says he approved Vance's Iran outreach
world.b: Al Jazeera's live coverage of the Iran war: Trump says he approved Vance's outreach to Iran over 'medical supplies'.
world.title: Trump says he approved Vance’s outreach to Iran over ‘medical supplies’

national.h: 30 years in prison for Minnesota food fraud
national.b: Salim Said was sentenced for a key role in defrauding a federal food program during the pandemic, in a case that drew attacks from Trump.
national.title: US man gets 30-year sentence for Minnesota fraud that drew Trump backlash

national.h: Hackers expose identities of 40,000-plus DHS staff
national.b: A hacktivist group said it subverted DHS's single sign-on system, exposing names, phone numbers and addresses, including of people in undercover operations.
national.title: Hackers expose the identities of more than 40,000 DHS employees

national.h: HHS to let pharmacies make popular peptides
national.b: HHS will exercise enforcement discretion for a half dozen wellness peptides made by compounding pharmacies, though evidence for their safety and effectiveness is sparse.

national.h: Federal judge Alvin Hellerstein dies at 92
national.b: The judge, who handled cases on Trump, Maduro and 9/11, died Wednesday morning; two weeks ago he presided over the Maduros' arraignment on torture charges.
national.title: Alvin Hellerstein, federal judge who handled cases on Trump, Maduro and 9/11, dies at 92

national.h: Labor icon Dolores Huerta dies at 96
national.b: Huerta co-founded the United Farm Workers union and coined the phrase "Sí, se puede!" Her family said she died Wednesday at home.

national.h: ICE partnerships with local police double
national.b: More than 29,000 state and local officers were deputized by ICE under the 287(g) program between January 2025 and October 2026, a report from FWD.us found.

politics.h: Trump calls for prosecution of Mary Peltola
politics.b: Trump said Peltola should be prosecuted after a New York Times report that her campaign discussed recruiting another candidate named Dan Sullivan in the Alaska Senate race.
politics.title: Trump calls for prosecution of Alaska Senate candidate Peltola over Sullivan name controversy

politics.h: Iran war cost to US taxpayers hits $47.1 billion
politics.b: The U.S. Central Command estimate, as of Oct. 16, is up $3.5 billion since early September, as the war's cost becomes a midterm issue.

politics.h: How Cleta Mitchell built an election movement
politics.b: ProPublica: The conservative election lawyer, who holds no formal administration role, has pressed the Trump administration to take actions before the midterms that even some allies say go too far.
politics.title: How Cleta Mitchell Turned Trump’s “Big Lie” Into a Movement

international.h: Activists say settlers beat them in West Bank
international.b: Activist Adele Shoko said armed settlers attacked her, US journalist Jasper Nathaniel and activist Andrey X in Umm al-Khair, and that Nathaniel was then arrested.
international.title: Activists accuse Israeli settlers of assault in occupied West Bank

international.h: King Charles faces slavery reckoning in Caribbean
international.b: Facing demands for an apology and reparations, Charles is expected to call slavery an "atrocity that forever stains our history" while stopping short of an apology.
international.title: King Charles III can't escape Britain's role in slavery as he tours Caribbean nations

international.h: Russell Brand denies all charges at trial
international.b: Brand, 51, testified at Southwark Crown Court, answering "no" to three counts of rape, three of sexual assault and one of attempted indecent assault.
international.title: Russell Brand denies all charges as he testifies at his rape and sex assault trial

international.h: Spain high-speed train crash kills at least 68
international.b: A high-speed train struck the rear of a stopped train near Urda in Toledo province; about 80 people were injured, 15 critically, the regional government says.
international.title: Train crash in Spain kills at least 68 people

international.h: US cruise ship ends world voyage over fuel costs
international.b: The Odyssey suspended operations in Cambodia, forcing hundreds of passengers to abandon their floating homes after fuel costs surged during the war in Iran.
Nassib, Jordan's only border crossing with Syria, reopens after Jordanian strikes on suspected ISIL sites killed at least seven people in southern Syria.

international.h: No winner yet in Israel's Netanyahu-Eisenkot race
international.b: Al Jazeera's live coverage: Results show no winner yet in the race between the Netanyahu and Eisenkot blocs.

international.h: Flavio Bolsonaro lands in Miami after election loss
international.b: The Brazilian senator and his family, granted US visas after he refused a Supreme Court order to surrender his passports, flew via Argentina and Ecuador after losing to Lula.

business.b: The Federal Reserve under Chairman Kevin Warsh opted not to raise rates after a September hike, saying "inflation remains elevated" amid an energy price spike tied to the Iran war.

business.h: Lawsuit challenges freeze on new ACA brokers
business.b: Federal officials stopped licensing new health insurance brokers weeks before open enrollment, citing fraud, hurting agencies that hired staff for the busy season.
business.title: Lawsuit challenges freeze on new health insurance brokers ahead of open enrollment

science.h: Strong El Niño points to warmer, wetter winter
science.b: NOAA forecasts warmer-than-average temperatures across much of the continental U.S., with above-average precipitation in several regions.
science.title: Forecasters are predicting a warmer and wetter winter. Here's how El Niño will affect your region

science.h: Western states lost a third of glacial cover
science.b: Six western states have lost more than one-third of their glacial cover since 1950 and more than 300 glaciers have disappeared, a Portland State and USGS analysis finds.

sports.h: Brewers win first World Series title
sports.b: Jacob Misiorowski threw 5 2/3 scoreless innings and Milwaukee beat Tampa Bay 4-1 in Game 5; William Contreras was named World Series MVP.
sports.title: Brewers beat the Rays to win the first World Series title in franchise history

sports.b: Kansas City signed the former Ravens kicker to its practice squad; Baltimore released Tucker in May 2025 after allegations of sexual misconduct.

sports.h: Rays rally in 12th to force World Series Game 5
sports.b: Jonny DeLuca and pinch-hitter Ben Williamson singled home runs in the 12th as Tampa Bay beat Milwaukee 4-3 to stave off elimination.

sports.h: Anthony Edwards to have knee surgery
sports.b: The Timberwolves star is headed for surgery on his right knee, with December the target for his return, per The Athletic, after scoring 47 points Monday in an overtime loss to Cleveland.
Indianapolis is sending the defensive tackle back to the team that drafted him for a 2027 fourth-round pick, according to ESPN. The Colts also dealt Quenton Nelson to the Seahawks.

local.h: Woman charged with hate crimes in stabbings of Jewish men
local.b: Federal prosecutors accuse Anna Mochalova, 32, of stabbing two Jewish men near the Diamond District with a sharp object consistent with a needle.
local.title: Woman charged with federal hate crimes after allegedly stabbing 2 Jewish men in NYC

local.h: E-bike battery caused fatal Bronx fire, FDNY says
local.b: The fire at the Patterson Houses in Mott Haven killed an 11-year-old boy and critically injured four other people early Wednesday.
local.title: Lithium-ion battery caused Bronx fire that killed 11-year-old, FDNY says

local.h: NYPD promises tight NYC Marathon security
local.b: Drones, dogs, horses and helicopters will watch the race; Commissioner Jessica Tisch said there are "no known specific credible threats."
local.title: 60K runners, 2.5 million fans: NYPD promises tight security for NYC Marathon

local.h: Brooklyn's Third Avenue to get safety redesign
local.b: The city will replace traffic lanes with bike lanes and shorten crossings on 2.1 miles of Third Avenue in Sunset Park, two months after nurse Jiayi Zheng was killed by a hit-and-run driver.
local.title: Mamdani plans redesign of Brooklyn's Third Avenue after nurse killed in hit-and-run

local.h: Board delays vote on Tompkins Square overhaul
local.b: Community Board 3 put off its vote on the $10 million Tompkins Square Park update until next month after preservationists protested over the park's pull-up bars.
local.title: 'If this is what you want': East Village board halts vote on Tompkins Square overhaul

periods.text: Partly cloudy, with a low around 58. Southwest wind 9 to 11 mph.

periods.text: Sunny, with a high near 69. Northwest wind 10 to 17 mph.

periods.name: Friday Night
periods.text: Mostly clear, with a low around 50. Northwest wind 10 to 14 mph.

periods.name: Saturday Night
periods.text: Mostly cloudy, with a low around 49.
